name: Healthcare
summary: Digital healthcare solutions for better patient care.
description: Healthcare UI UX design for patient apps, booking, records, telehealth and clinical dashboards: accessible products that patients and clinicians can trust.
image_alt: Doctor working at a laptop, healthcare industry
overview:
Healthcare products are used by people who are often anxious, unwell or short of time. Patients need to book, check results and manage their care without confusion, and clinicians need the right information without extra clicks. Plain language, accessible design and clear status at every step matter more here than almost anywhere.

I work with founders and product teams on web and mobile health products, from the first prototype to a design system that engineers can build from directly. On MediCare, I turned a 9-step booking flow into three taps. Privacy, consent and accessibility are part of the design from day one.

challenges.title: Accessibility for everyone
challenges.text: Patients of every age and ability need readable text, clear contrast and screens that work with assistive tools.

challenges.title: Booking friction
challenges.text: Long forms and unclear availability make patients give up before they book.

challenges.title: Clinician time
challenges.text: Busy staff need key patient information at a glance, not spread across many screens.

challenges.title: Privacy and consent
challenges.text: Sensitive data, permissions and consent have to be clear without slowing care down.

faqs.question: Do you have experience designing healthcare products?
faqs.answer: Yes. I designed MediCare, a patient booking app that turned a 9-step booking flow into three taps. You can see the case study on this page.

faqs.question: How do you design for accessibility?
faqs.answer: I follow WCAG guidelines for contrast, text size, focus states and screen reader support, and check key flows with assistive tools before handoff.

faqs.question: How do you handle patient privacy in the design?
faqs.answer: I work with your team to map what data each screen needs, then design clear consent, permission and sign-in steps. Your legal and compliance team still sets the final rules.

faqs.question: Do you design for both patients and clinicians?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many health products need a patient app and a staff dashboard, so I design both on one shared system.

faqs.question: How do we start?
faqs.answer: Send me a short brief through the contact page. We will have a call about your product, users and timeline, and I will come back with a plan and quote.
